 Paralympian Ezra Frech shares 'motivating factor' for potential history-making DWTS win
 Lauren DuBois Updated 2026년 11월 2일 월 오후 11:56 UTC 0 Ezra Frech is opening up about what is motivating him to win Dancing With the Stars (Image: ABC) Ezra Frech has been making waves as a front-runner on Dancing With the Stars, and now, the Paralympian is opening up about what winning the show could really mean for him as he inches closer to the finals.
 The dance competition series , currently airing its 35th season on ABC , is just a few short weeks away from its finale, with only eight celebrities remaining in the competition thus far, including Frech, who is competing with Season 30 champion Daniella Karagach.
 While no one is safe, including on Disney Night, Frech has proven to be one of the most impactful stars of the season.

 The athlete, 21, has been impressing viewers of the show with his routines, which he has performed beautifully, and earned some of the season's top scores on, despite using a prosthetic leg and missing three fingers from his left hand.
 Now, in a new interview, he is opening up about what he hopes to achieve with his historic run on the show.
 Ezra Frech is opening up about what has him motivated to win DWTS (Image: ABC) Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter , Frech admitted he doesn't want to think too far ahead, because "anything could happen at any week," but that he does have high hopes for making the finale and potentially winning the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.
 "Of course, getting the opportunity to make the finale, to win the show, to get to represent the disabled community in that way and become the first amputee to win Dancing With the Stars would be very, very special, and would mean a lot to myself and hopefully to all people with disabilities and the community as a whole," he said.
 "That's the motivating factor; it's representing my people well, representing this contingent of the population that I feel hasn't had proper representation in mainstream media and doesn't feel maybe properly included in society," he added.
 Advertisement
 "That's the motivation for even being on the show in the first place, is [to] represent them well."
 If he wins, Frech would become the first amputee to ever win the show (Image: ABC) If Frech did win, he would make history on the show as the first-ever amputee to win the Mirrorball.
 While it would make history, he isn't the first to represent his community as a whole, as several others have represented the disabled community on the show over the years and have fared well in the competition.
 The first amputee to do the show was Heather Mills, who competed in season four, placing seventh overall. Amy Purdy was the next to do the show in Season 18, where she took second, followed by Noah Galloway in Season 20, who placed third.
 The show has also sought to give representation to the deaf community as well, with Marlee Matlin competing in Season 6, taking seventh, Nyle DiMarco winning Season 22, and Daniel Durant coming in fifth during Season 31.
 Dancing With the Stars airs Tuesdays on ABC and Disney+ .
